subject: Adaptive fallback guardrail activation — immediate verification requested
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Cho <hannah@blendanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Adaptive fallback guardrail activation — immediate verification requested

Hannah —

Quick note from our incident ops desk: during a brief runtime divergence at 13:42 PDT we observed degraded token accounting on one Dedicated pool that could cause incomplete KV cache hits for a small subset of long-prefix requests. Our engineers prepared an adaptive fallback guardrail that forces a KV-lookup bypass and short-circuits to a more conservative execution path while we roll a patch.

We will activate the guardrail in your us-west dedicated pool at 15:00 PDT. Expected customer-visible impact: transient 10–30ms extra tail latency for affected requests, no data loss, and no changes to inference outputs. Activation is short notice — we need a quick verification from your SRE/QA to confirm no unexpected client-side timeouts.

Required actions for Blend Analytics:
- Run the attached verification_script.sh against your staging traffic (instructions in the script) within 30 minutes of activation.
- Confirm whether your client-side timeout is <=500ms (if so, let us know and we can adjust a short deadline).
- If you see any failed requests after activation, capture the request IDs and send to sre@blendanalytics.com and cc us.

Attachments included: kv_fallback_patch.diff (patch), verification_script.sh (bash), customer_brief.pdf (short summary for legal/procurement).

We know this is short notice — Ben and Marissa are looped for credits/compensation coordination if the brief degradation blocks any SLA windows. Lauren will run the activation and follow up immediately with telemetry.

I'll confirm when the guardrail is live.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Hannah Cho <hannah@blendanalytics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@blendanalytics.com, sre@blendanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 14:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Adaptive fallback guardrail activation — immediate verification requested

Thanks Priya — appreciate the heads-up. A couple quick Qs from our SRE team: 

1) Does the guardrail change response shape or just latency? We need to be sure our upstream parsers won't mis-handle anything.
2) Can you confirm which pool nodes are affected (IDs or AZs) so our routing rules can skip them for short-lived traffic?

We're spinning up a quick staging run now and will execute verification_script.sh as soon as the guardrail is live. If our client-side timeouts are within default, we should be fine, but we'll report within 15 minutes of activation.

Hannah
Hannah Cho
SRE Lead, Blend Analytics
hannah@blendanalytics.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Adaptive fallback guardrail activation — immediate verification requested

Looping on compensation and comms. If Blend experiences any request failures during the guardrail window we'll offer a pro-rated credit against June usage; Marissa can confirm final wording. I also drafted a short customer-facing blurb in case they need to notify internal stakeholders (attached PDF).

Marissa — can you prepare a single-line ops note for their execs and a credit estimate?
Lauren — when you flip the guardrail, please paste the telemetry link and the node IDs here.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Cho <hannah@blendanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, sre@blendanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 15:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Adaptive fallback guardrail activation — immediate verification requested

Hannah —

Guardrail is active as of 15:47 PDT on nodes: us-west-2a-{node-73}, us-west-2b-{node-81}. It only forces the conservative execution path (no output changes expected) — the only observable difference should be the +10–25ms tail on long-prefix KV routes. Telemetry dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood.com/incident/2028-06-05/fallback-activation (internal link).

We ran the verification script across a 2000-rpm staging replay and saw no errors. Please run the same script against your staging; if you see failures, include the request IDs (we'll correlate).

Marissa — estimated credit if their production windows were affected (per our SLOs) is ~0.8% of June committed spend, pending procurement sign-off.

Hannah — thanks again for the rapid response. If you want us to rollback the guardrail instead of running through the patch, say the word and we'll revert immediately. Otherwise we'll follow with a durable patch tonight and a postmortem for your security team by EOD tomorrow.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
